messages:
Irene Cho: Quick thread — we need a clear design for credential provenance across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Main ask: be able to answer \"who created this key, what was it created for, and which runtime used it\".
Sam Turner: Are we talking mint-time metadata only or continuous per-request attribution?
Irene Cho: Both. Mint metadata must be immutable and searchable; runtime should trace a request back to the issuance record.
Ravi Patel: Two feasible patterns: 1) opaque token + issuance record in DB (introspectable), 2) self-contained signed token with embedded claims.
Marta Gomez: Signed tokens avoid DB hits on every request. But revocation is hard unless TTLs are tiny or we maintain a revocation list.
Alex Rivera: Opaque + cache is operationally straightforward. Runtimes cache issuance rows with TTL. On cache miss, introspect to broker. But at 50-200k rps this caching layer needs sizing.
Sam Turner: Hybrid idea: token carries a compact signed issuance statement (issuance_id + signer sig). Runtimes verify signature locally (JWKS) to confirm authenticity, then use issuance_id to enrich or check revocation via cached metadata.
Ravi Patel: I like hybrid. Signature verifies origin without DB; issuance_id allows us to attach audit and admin metadata later. Revocation path: cache + async refresh + on-demand introspect.
Marta Gomez: Operational rules proposal:
- Default token lifetime: hosted 1h, dedicated 8h (configurable), private: customer-settable.
- Mint payload fields: issuance_id, issuer, created_by, org_id, project_id, intended_use, issued_at, exp, aud.
- Token format: opaque bearer string that base64-encodes compact payload and signature (keeps flexibility). Keep payload < 512 bytes.
Alex Rivera: For impersonation / act-as flows, include parent_issuance_id reference (single immediate parent). Full chain stored in issuance-store; runtimes fetch chain only when policy evaluation requires it. Limit depth to avoid token bloat.
Sam Turner: Mint-time policy enforcement is critical. Broker must enforce who can create tokens for which org/project and record approval metadata for cross-project issuance. Runtime should treat admin-minted tokens differently (require extra checks).
Ravi Patel: Key rotation: broker rotates signing keys (publish JWKS). Runtimes must accept past keys for grace period. Audit store keeps original issuance record (signed) so we can prove provenance long-term.
Marta Gomez: Private deployments: support customer-signed issuance or broker-forwarding. For customer-signed, we accept customer's JWKS; for broker-forwarding, broker mints on behalf and stores mapping to customer artifact. Document tradeoffs in RFC.
Alex Rivera: Danger: trusting project_id claim mechanically. If some service can mint arbitrary project_id, we open privilege escalation. So require mint-time checks and attach a \"minted_by_policy\" flag in issuance metadata.
Sam Turner: Metrics to track: issuance cache hit rate, introspection qps, signature verification p50/p99 latency, token TTL histogram, revocation propagation lag.
Ravi Patel: Auditability: append canonical issuance records to WORM store (S3 + immutability) and store issuance_id in token. That allows offline reconstruction even if runtime cache flushed.
Marta Gomez: Example compact issuance payload: 
{ 
  "issuance_id": "iss_2a9d...", 
  "issuer": "token-broker-03", 
  "created_by": "service:repo-deploy", 
  "org_id": "org-12", 
  "project_id": "proj-77", 
  "intended_use": "inference:client", 
  "aud": "model-serving", 
  "iat": 1701234567, 
  "exp": 1701238167 
}
signature = sign(payload, broker_sk)
Token = base64(payload) + "." + base64(signature) + "." + random_nonce

Irene Cho: Action items:
- Marta: draft mint payload schema + JWKS rotation + edge cases for private (PR by Tue)
- Alex: perf/cost estimate for runtime cache sizing and signature verify latency (data points for 100k rps)
- Sam: define mint-time RBAC rules and admin token markers + approval flow sketch
- Ravi: spec audit-store layout and chain reconstruction API (how to fetch full parent chain)

KeyBot: FYI: security-checklist updated. When RFC lands tag @eng-security and include threat-model section.

Irene Cho: Great. I'll draft RFC for hybrid issuance format and include the above action items. Thanks everyone.
